classification.difficultyReason: Identify named circle features and distinguish major and minor arcs in a supplied diagram.

content.prompt: In the diagram on the right, name:

spec.description: Circle centred at O, with clockwise circumference order U, T, S, R. RT and US are diameters; RS and ST are additional chords. Ordinary source blue lines and red centre marker are rendered in house black.
spec.mathematics: R and T are opposite endpoints, as are U and S. The centre lies on both diameters. No lengths or angle measurements are supplied.
spec.answerVisibility: All geometry and labels are permanent student-visible givens; no answers are added.

answer.worked: $O$ is the centre, where the two diameters intersect.
$RT$ and $SU$ each join two points on the circle and pass through the centre $O$, so both are diameters.

children.label: c
children.prompt: two chords that are not diameters

answer.worked: $RS$ and $ST$ each join two points on the circle but do not pass through $O$, so they are chords that are not diameters.
$OR$, $OU$, $OT$ and $OS$ each join the centre to a point on the circle, so each is a radius.

answer.short: Any one of the arcs $SRT$, $RUS$, $UTR$ or $TSU$.
answer.worked: For example, arc $SRT$ is the larger curved part between $S$ and $T$, passing through $R$. The other valid major arcs are $RUS$, $UTR$ and $TSU$.

answer.short: Any one of the minor arcs $RS$, $RU$, $UT$ or $TS$.
answer.worked: For example, minor arc $RS$ is the smaller curved part between $R$ and $S$. The other valid minor arcs are $RU$, $UT$ and $TS$.
